question: What does the official 2015 Labac-Alemang watershed assessment abstract establish, and can it resolve a river boundary or provide fish records?

source.title: Biophysical Characterization and Vulnerability Assessment of the Labac-Alemang River Watershed, Cavite, Philippines
source.citation: December 2015 report; a mirrored CvSU research listing gives the project period May–October 2015 and names DENR-PENRO Cavite and CvSU as project leaders.

access.method: Officially hosted PDF abstract text and metadata were reviewed online. The indexed view returned only abstract text; no full report, map annex, local PDF or geometry file was obtained.

findings.abstractReports: The report used GIS mapping, field survey, biodiversity and water-quality assessment to characterize the Labac-Alemang River Watershed. It says relevant maps were generated to support an Integrated Watershed Management Plan and notes watershed vulnerabilities. Its biodiversity statement identifies a giant cloud rat concern, not fish taxa.
findings.waterbodyIdentity: This is watershed-level identity context. It does not establish the boundary of the Labac River channel, equate slash-delimited river labels, or resolve the 2023 provincial-profile table omissions.
findings.geometry: No coordinates, CRS, polygon, stream centerline or map annex contents were present in the reviewed abstract.
findings.fishEvidence: The abstract contains no fish inventory, station-level fish result, fish occurrence, gear, sampling date or fish voucher.
findings.authorOverlap: J. N. Panizales is named in this 2015 report and in a separate secondary 2014 fish-presentation listing. The overlap is a search lead only; the source records do not establish that the works are related or that the contributor identity is the same.

rightsAndUse.decision: The official public host does not itself grant an open license. Keep abstract-level metadata in the research ledger only; do not reproduce maps or report content without checking item-specific terms.

nextAction: Seek the full report and map annex through public or authorized DENR-PENRO or CvSU repositories if watershed-level context is needed. Keep this record separate from the 2014 fish presentation and from Labac channel geometry.
